neighbours.label: K-12 schooling jargon: ' gifted' said of students/learners/children (also co-teaching, special education); not 'gifted' as personal talent, a gift, or higher/adult education
fire: Our elementary school screens every second grader for the gifted program in the spring.
Many teachers say they lack the time to plan separate lessons for gifted pupils.
The workshop showed new teachers how to challenge gifted students in a mixed classroom.
A magnet school for gifted children opened in the district two years ago.
The principal asked how the curriculum could be adapted for gifted learners in fourth grade.
The two co-teaching partners shared one classroom and planned each unit together.
Research on gifted students suggests they benefit from faster pacing in math.
The district moved several special education students into general education classrooms.
quiet: The orchestra hired a gifted cellist who had trained in Vienna.
My grandmother was a gifted storyteller and a patient listener.
He bought a small gift for his teacher at the end of the year.
The university expanded its higher education programs for working adults.
The principal asked how the cafeteria menu could be improved for fourth graders.
A new swimming pool for local children opened in the district two years ago.
The workshop showed new nurses how to handle difficult patients on a busy ward.
The talented young goalkeeper was signed by the club last summer.

notes: Card: top examples are gifted students, Gifted Child Quarterly, co-teaching, general education. Probes: 'gifted students/learners/children' 0.53-0.67, 'gifted pianist/striker' 0.13, 'higher/adult education' ~0.01, 'special education' 0.31-0.43.
